notes: Mun's figures: the lesson says 'In one year England exported goods worth £2.2 million and imported £2.0 million, keeping a net gain of £200,000' without saying these are Mun's own example figures; the question source_note attributes them correctly ('figures from Mun's own example in the same chapter'). Minor attribution softness; figures themselves are correct as Mun's example. No student would answer a question wrong because of it.

MCQ 0266 key option B ('English colonists largely avoided contact or relations with Native Americans as much as possible') overstates avoidance: the English displaced Native peoples through sustained contact (trade, war, land-taking), and the item's own rationale says 'trade when they had to, fight when they chose to'. The key is unambiguous by elimination (A, C, D are all contradicted by the stimulus) and the stimulus's 'rather than living or working alongside them' supports it, so this is a wording note, not a fail. 'Kept their distance / separated rather than lived alongside' would be accurate.

Style inconsistency (not a fail): Topic 2.5 key rationales run 60-90 words (some 4 sentences: 0255, 0258, 0267, 0272, 0273, 0277), against the spec's 'Key note: 1-3 short sentences' and against Unit 1 / Topic 2.4 practice (key rationales 10-40 words). The validator passes them (its line bound counts newline-separated lines), the content is accurate, and the length line 'key explanation 60-120 words' arguably supports them — so this is a consistency note for the parent, not a defect.

Images viewed with my own eye and stimulus descriptions verified accurate: Bowen chart (trade winds twice, 'seat of war' title), Brookes (454 allowed, 292 lower deck, 2 feet 7 inches), Kip Elmina (canoes, fort, caption A/B as quoted), Fumagalli (master's house upper left, quarters below, works at right, one person fishing in the foreground, no one working the cane), Havana (harbor, ships, palms, city on far shore, February 1765 imprint), Darley (warriors with tomahawks, settler firing musket, frightened child center, fallen settler foreground), Smith map (Native towns named, Powhatan enthroned inset with the 1607 caption, Native man with bow at right, royal arms center), Jan Beary Jamestown (sick settler carried, dejected man on cannon, grave being dug).
